effect_mechanism: Reviews report that under drought understorey crop yields could be higher than in an open system even in intense shade, that trees and live fences supply livestock fodder when pasture is scarce, and that agroforestry biomass production varied less over four years than conventional systems in semi-arid Brazil, attributed to water availability [ev_drought_hazard_dobhal24_13, ev_drought_hazard_dobhal24_14, ev_drought_hazard_moran18_1, ev_drought_hazard_santos25_6]. In an eastern Canadian soybean intercrop, experimentally induced drought caused crop losses in the monocrop only [ev_drought_hazard_ipccar6ch5_4].

justification.conditionality: The 59.2% infiltration figure from another meta-analysis aggregates agroforestry with perennial grasses and managed forestry, the recharge benefit holds at moderate density, and the rainfall shift with upwind tree cover is a continental-scale effect [ev_soil_permeability_basche19_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ipccar6_1, ev_water_regulation_vannoordwijk21_4]. No unit measures water stress directly, and the IPCC infiltration statement draws on the same pantropical meta-analysis [ev_soil_permeability_ipccar6_1, ev_soil_permeability_muchane20_1].

effect_mechanism: Combining canopy interception and transpiration of trees with their effects on infiltration, Ilstedt et al. derived an optimal intermediate tree density for parklands from a groundwater-recharge perspective [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_vannoordwijk21_6].
conditionality: The relationship is non-monotonic, so more trees is not always better for recharge, and it is a cited modelling result used as a component of water stress with no measured water-stress outcome [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_vannoordwijk21_6].
